key_finding: The task premise is wrong: GAP9 GCC never accepts a true run-time normalisation/clip argument and has no register form for them (function parameter or global -> 'invalid argument to built-in function on arg N', at every -O level; any non-literal at -O0). It accepts values that become constant after its optimisation (local variable, const/static variable, parameter of an inlined always_inline function) and then applies the same range rules as for literals. That is exactly the SDK pattern (int Prec=10; gap_mulsN(...,Prec) in fp16 CNN kernels; OUT_CLIP(acc, OutUnsigned, OutDatasize) inside an always_inline NE16 kernel). So the fix defers the check to instruction selection (after LLVM optimisation) instead of adding a run-time lowering.
design_choice: New .deferred intrinsics used only when an immediate is not an ICE, rather than dropping ImmArg from the existing intrinsics: ImmArg is what prevents SimplifyCFG/GVNSink from merging calls with different constant immediates into a phi (Local.cpp canReplaceOperandWithVariable), so dropping it could newly break literal calls. With this design every call that compiled before takes the identical path (verified: same IR/asm/diagnostics). Mechanism reference: upstream 846e562dcc6a '[Clang] add support for error+warning fn attrs' (GCC-compatible post-optimisation diagnostics via a backend DiagnosticInfo); DiagnosticInfoUnsupported as in upstream RISCVISelLowering.cpp:20596 @llvmorg-20.1.8. Scope: mul/mac {s,u,hhs,hhu}{N,RN} + clip/clipu (task scope); addN/subN/bextract/binsert etc. still require literals (GCC also folds those, e.g. addN/bextract with a local variable compile in GCC) - not needed by the SDK survey, left as a possible follow-up.
gcc_rules_mirrored: post-optimisation constant required; Norm <= 31 (unsigned); RN: 1 <= Norm <= 31 and Round == 2^(Norm-1) (GCC rejects Norm = 0 for RN); clip: Min = -2^(N-1), Max = 2^(N-1)-1, clipu: Min = 0, 1 <= N <= 30 (same as F011's Sema rule).

other_errors_seen: Pre-existing: literal __builtin_pulp_{mul,mac}{s,u,hhs,hhu}RN(..., 0, 1) is accepted by our Sema (round = 1<<0) and emits p.*RN ...,0, but GAP9 GCC rejects Norm = 0 for every RN builtin ('expects Norm and Round cst, Norm<=31, Round==2^(Norm-1)'). Left unchanged (task: keep the constant checks); the new deferred path follows GCC and rejects Norm = 0.

GAP9 GCC bug: every __builtin_pulp_mulhh{s,u}[R]N / machh{s,u}[R]N call fails with 'invalid argument to built-in function on arg 1, builtin arg mode: SI, actual arg mode: HI', even with literals. Not our issue; noted for the GCC-bug list.

GAP9 GCC also folds post-optimisation constants for other immediate builtins (addN with a local variable -> p.addN, bextract -> p.extract); ours still require literals there. No SDK file in the survey needs it.
Diagnostics from the back end point at the function (no line) without -g, unlike Sema errors.
